protocol.warmup: Standalone 5 VUs / 10 seconds after cold smoke: 162 requests, 0 errors; p95=845.246ms. Warm-up results excluded from experiments.
protocol.workload: Each VU iterates catalog GET then unique-idempotency-key order POST; 50 ms think time, 8 s request timeout, 10 s graceful completion.
protocol.phases: BEFORE degraded; AFTER restored; workload configuration identical within each experiment.
protocol.durability: MySQL defaults retained; named persistent Docker volume; no fsync relaxation.
protocol.concurrency: Benchmarks run sequentially after integration suites stopped. Background outbox delivery persists across scenarios; zero-backlog gate before Kafka.
protocol.runnerPreflight: The measurements predate the automated three-sample idle guard. Kafka used an explicit zero-outbox/zero-lag gate with its drain samples retained; other scenarios were sequential without this gate. Subsequent comparison runners enforce three idle observations before activation.

limitations: One run per scenario; no statistical significance or production capacity claim.
Closed-loop constant-VU traffic reduces offered load when requests slow. Actual counts differ between phases.

Mixed percentiles combine two routes; the order route dominates the mixed p95 on this host; commit/disk overhead is a candidate cause that was not isolated by profiling. Separate route diagnostics are provided.
Database degradation bypasses cache and executes 51 SQL operations per logical catalog lookup; restored mode enables cache and batched SQL. This comparison does not isolate the independent effects.
DB lookup count counts logical loads, not individual SQL statements; DB p95 measures whole logical lookup.
Global outbox/consumer-lag gauges can include prior sessions; phase-scoped worker counts represent completed processing at snapshot time and may be incomplete while outbox drains.
Redis/catalog database work is cheap on the 50-row catalog page from 10,000 seeded products; less database work need not increase end-to-end throughput.
Trace identifiers from core-profile measurement exports are correlation references; Tempo export is disabled for these measurements. Instrumented trace proof is a separate validation run.
